items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-09-08
items.q: Sidney Bichet. Well, that's the kind of style of clan that I like.

ctx.x: I've never heard him play clan in there.
Sidney Bichet. Well, that's the kind of style of clan that I like. What about Sport?
He... Yeah, Sport was all right.

items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: But I always got that idea from Bechet and them fellas, you know.

ctx.x: That's the same guy who used to work with Dewey Jackson? Might have been.

I know he's from way around St. Louis. Yeah, well they played on St. Louis. Yeah, he had a four octave I think of Viperphone. No, he wasn't a Viperphone, remember. Yeah. And then he could play piano too. He was a wonderful drummer. Well I took some lessons for him. But see, after he, I was a fellow to advance fast. I took lessons on the clarinet too, but a fellow wanted to take me away from him because I, I used to, that sit out, you see the method to make the clarinet now, is very simplified. You notice all the…
You were talking about Sidney that day.

items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: we had a little band. I went and got some skin off a round steak and dried it and made a drum. My brother had a corn and a piece of silver pig on it. And he would play there like a trumpet. And Bichet, he had the flute.

ctx.x: Well, anyhow, I'll get back on Joe Lewis while he came to me. He got, Sidney, he was another fella who played that little fight. He, another fella, could play a fight. So, we, I'll tell you how we had, we had a little band. I went and got some skin off a round steak and dried it and made a drum. My brother had a corn and a piece of silver pig on it. And he would play there like a trumpet. And Bichet, he had the flute. And another fella, well, he turned out to be a garbage court driver. He turned out to be a…
Yeah, that's right. That's back at that time. When would that have been, do you think? Oh, yeah.
